sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain sung by Leo Moll. “Spiel’ mir auf der Balalaika einen russischen Tango.” Electrola E.G. 2392, matrix 00499-1; recorded in Berlin, 18 August 1931, released October 1931; also issued as His Master’s Voice AM 3741. Session and issue data from the Electrola label list at musiktiteldb.de, based on the Discographie der deutschen Tanzmusik. Digital transfer on YouTube, video Oq4sWv9khw4.
sources.title: Spiel’ mir auf der Balalaika einen russischen Tango — Electrola E.G. 2392
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester; Leo Moll, vocal refrain
sources.researchNote: The transfer description dates the recording to 1932, whereas the Electrola label list gives a Berlin session on 18 August 1931 and an October 1931 release. The session-based chronology is preferred.

sources.shortCitation: Domgraf-Fassbaender, “Tränen in der Geige” (Jube Pops reissue, via YouTube)
sources.fullCitation: Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender with the Marek Weber Orchestra conducted by Marek Weber. “Ich will dich Liebe lehren: Tranen in der Geige.” Music by Bronisław Kaper and Walter Jurmann; words by Fritz Rotter. On Schlager und Filmmelodien von Walter Jurmann, vol. 1 (Recordings 1930–1938). Jube Pops, released 5 February 2013; YouTube art track supplied by Naxos Digital Services and published 11 February 2015.
sources.title: Tränen in der Geige — Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender, Jube Pops reissue
sources.creator: Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender; Marek Weber Orchestra, Marek Weber, conductor
sources.researchNote: The digital reissue does not identify the label, catalogue number or matrix of the original disc.

sources.shortCitation: Domgraf-Fassbaender, “Schön ist das ganze Leben” (Jube Pops reissue, via YouTube)
sources.fullCitation: Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender with the Marek Weber Orchestra conducted by Marek Weber. “Der gluckliche Herr Funf: Schon ist das ganze Leben.” Music by Bronisław Kaper and Walter Jurmann; words by Fritz Rotter. On Schlager und Filmmelodien von Walter Jurmann, vol. 2 (Recordings 1929–1936). Jube Pops, released 5 February 2013; YouTube art track supplied by Naxos Digital Services and published 11 February 2015.
sources.title: Schön ist das ganze Leben — Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender, Jube Pops reissue
sources.creator: Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender; Marek Weber Orchestra, Marek Weber, conductor
sources.researchNote: The digital reissue does not identify the label, catalogue number or matrix of the original disc.

sources.shortCitation: His Master’s Voice (Electrola), “Tränen weint jede Frau so gern”
sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain sung by Austin Egen. “Tränen weint jede Frau so gern.” Tango. His Master’s Voice / Electrola, 1929. Digital transfer on YouTube.
sources.title: Tränen weint jede Frau so gern — His Master’s Voice (Electrola)
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Refraingesang: Austin Egen
sources.researchNote: The year, Nico Dostal’s arrangement credit, Kaper’s music credit and Fritz Rotter’s words credit are supplied by the upload description. The disc label is not shown, so these details are not treated as a label transcription.

sources.shortCitation: Electrola E.G. 2271, “Du lieber Geiger, spiel’ einen Tango für mich” (Marek Weber, 1931)
sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester. “Du lieber Geiger, spiel’ einen Tango für mich.” Electrola E.G. 2271, matrix OD267-1, recorded in Berlin on 24 March 1931 and released June 1931. Digital transfer published on YouTube by 78rpm Musik on 27 April 2025; discographic data from the Electrola label list at musiktiteldb.de.
sources.title: Du lieber Geiger, spiel’ einen Tango für mich — Electrola E.G. 2271
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester
sources.researchNote: The Electrola label list, drawing on the Discographie der deutschen Tanzmusik, describes the side as instrumental. This conflicts with the transfer description, which calls it a dance-orchestra recording with refrain vocal. The label is not shown in the upload.

sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain credited as Leo Moll. “Signorina aus Brioni.” Tango; label credits Fritz Rotter and Dr. Kaper for music and text. Electrola E.G. 2400, n.d. Shellac disc, Radiomuseum Hardthausen / Schallarchiv; filmed-label transfer on YouTube.
sources.title: Signorina aus Brioni — Electrola E.G. 2400
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Refrain: Leo Moll
sources.researchNote: The uploader identifies the singer credited as Leo Moll as Leo Monosson, gives 1931 as the issue year and accompanies the transfer with a 1930 photograph of Brioni. These details are not printed on the filmed label.

sources.shortCitation: Electrola EG 2508, “Du bist in meinem Leben die erste Sensation”
sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, vocal by John Hendrik. “Du bist in meinem Leben die erste Sensation.” Tango. Electrola E.G. 2508, 1932. Digital transfer on YouTube.
sources.title: Du bist in meinem Leben die erste Sensation — Electrola EG 2508
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Gesang: John Hendrik
sources.researchNote: An uploader-created opening card gives matrix E-OD 795 / I and a recording date of 17 February 1932. The disc label is not shown and the card contains no authorship credits; the matrix and date are therefore description-level evidence, not a label transcription.

sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, dance orchestra with refrain vocal. “Margarete, wander mit mir ….” Fox-trot; label credits music and text to Fritz Rotter and Dr. B. Kaper. Electrola E.G. 2406, matrix 60-1740, n.d. Shellac disc, Radiomuseum Hardthausen / Schallarchiv; filmed-label transfer on YouTube.
sources.title: Margarete, wander mit mir … — Electrola E.G. 2406
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Tanz-Orchester mit Refraingesang
sources.researchNote: The uploader dates the Electrola recording to 1931 and links an Italian version by the Orchestra da Ballo del R. Culotta. These contextual details are not printed on the filmed label.

sources.fullCitation: König, Henry, comp. “Labelliste von „Electrola“ (1930–1934), Labelcode 00193: Labelnummern von EG 2000 bis EG 2990.” musiktiteldb.de. 422 sides recorded, with matrix numbers, recording dates and studios, release months and parallel issues, compiled from the Discographie der deutschen Tanzmusik, the Discographie der deutschen Kleinkunst and contemporary trade documents.
sources.title: Labelliste „Electrola“ (1930–1934), EG 2000–EG 2990
sources.creator: Henry König, compiler

sources.shortCitation: Electrola EG 2135, “Ach, Otto, Otto…!” (Marek Weber with Siegfried Arno, 1931)
sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain sung by Siegfried Arno. “Ach, Otto, Otto…!” Foxtrot; Electrola EG 2135, matrix BD 9264-2, playing time 3:12; recorded in the Beethoven-Saal, Berlin, and released in January 1931; also issued as His Master’s Voice AM 3450. Music by Bronisław Kaper, words by Fritz Rotter. Entry in the Electrola label list and the title list at musiktiteldb.de, both following the Discographie der deutschen Kleinkunst, vol. 1.
sources.title: Ach, Otto, Otto…! — Electrola EG 2135
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester; Siegfried Arno, refrain vocal

sources.fullCitation: HeadHunter131, uploader. “Siegfried Arno: Ach Otto Otto!” YouTube audio reference, uploaded 11 August 2008.
sources.title: Siegfried Arno: Ach Otto Otto! — Sig Arno, YouTube
sources.creator: HeadHunter131
sources.researchNote: The upload gives no label, catalogue or matrix number. Discographic literature records a single Siegfried Arno performance of the song: Electrola E.G. 2135 with Marek Weber und sein Orchester.

sources.shortCitation: Electrola E.G. 2532, “Ganz ohne Liebe wär’ das Leben so bescheiden”
sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester. “Ganz ohne Liebe wär’ das Leben so bescheiden.” Fox-trot with refrain vocal; label credits music to Jurmann and Kaper and words to Fritz Rotter. Electrola E.G. 2532, 1932. Digital transfer on YouTube.
sources.title: Ganz ohne Liebe wär’ das Leben so bescheiden — Electrola E.G. 2532
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester
sources.researchNote: The upload description gives matrix OD 879-2, places the session in Berlin around March 1932 and tentatively suggests John Hendrik as the refrain singer. The label is not shown, and the singer identification remains unconfirmed.
